title: Test command: logical operators -a, -o, \! not working
description:
The following test command logical operators don't work:
- `[ 1 -eq 1 -a 2 -eq 2 ]` returns 1 instead of 0
- `[ 1 -eq 1 -o 2 -eq 3 ]` returns 1 instead of 0
- `[ ! 1 -eq 2 ]` returns 1 instead of 0

**Root cause**: tree-sitter-bash parses these with wrong operator precedence:
- `[ 1 -eq 1 -a 2 -eq 2 ]` → `((1 -eq 1) -a 2) -eq 2` instead of `(1 -eq 1) -a (2 -eq 2)`
- `[ ! 1 -eq 2 ]` → `(!1) -eq 2` instead of `!(1 -eq 2)`

Fixing this would require patching tree-sitter-bash grammar or special-case rewriting in our interpreter.

title: Systematic bash node type test coverage
description:
Systematically test all bash node types and reduce test code duplication.

## Code Duplication Issue
All 9 test functions are nearly identical - only differ by test list name.
Refactor to single parametrized test or generate test functions dynamically.

## Node Type Coverage

### visit_* methods (statements/commands)
TESTED:
- command (echo, cat, true, false, exit)
- list (;, &&, ||)
- redirected_statement (heredocs)
- variable_assignment (inline with commands)

NOT TESTED:
- if_statement
- while_statement  
- for_statement
- c_style_for_statement
- case_statement
- function_definition
- pipeline (|)
- subshell ((...))
- negated_command (!)
- test_command ([[ ]])
- declaration_command (export, declare)
- unset_command

### evaluate_* methods (expressions)
TESTED:
- simple_expansion ($VAR)
- expansion (${VAR}, ${VAR:-default})
- ansi_c_string ($'...')
- word (with brace expansion)
- raw_string ('...')
- string ("...")
- heredoc_body, heredoc_content

NOT TESTED:
- arithmetic_expansion ($((...)))
- array
- binary_expression
- ternary_expression
- unary_expression
- postfix_expression
- command_substitution ($(...))
- concatenation
- subscript
- regex
- process_substitution (<(...))

title: [[ =~ ]] regex matching returns wrong results
description:
Regex matching in [[ ]] returns incorrect results:

- `[[ "hello123" =~ [0-9]+ ]]` returns 1 instead of 0 (should match)
- `[[ "abc" =~ ^a ]]` returns 1 instead of 0 (should match)

Seems to always return 1 (no match) even when regex should match.

title: Arithmetic: unary minus and bitwise NOT fail
description: Expressions like `(( x = -5 ))` and `(( x = ~5 ))` fail because the negative result is being interpreted as a command flag. The result '-5' or '-6' is passed to echo which treats it as an unknown flag.

title: Test command: [ = ] with quoted strings returns wrong result

Note: `!=` works correctly.
